lines: Earth stops spinning for one second.
But you keep moving at 465 metres per second.
At the equator, that's about 1,675 kilometres per hour, heading east.
Gravity pulls down at 9.8 metres per second squared.
Sideways, only the ground can slow you down.
At 45 degrees latitude, it's still about 1,184 kilometres per hour.
Only near the poles would the stop feel gentle.

traceability.purpose: Hook: the real globe turning (time-lapse, not to scale) stops dead on 'stops'; at once east-pointing arrows appear on every latitude: the ground halted, everything on it did not.

evidence.claim: Earth's rotational speed is about 1,674.7 km/h (465.2 m/s) at the equator, decreasing to zero at the poles.

traceability.purpose: Inertia: seen from the surface, nothing moves until the ground stops; then buildings and hills rush backwards while the person keeps the speed the ground had (the cited value labels the arrow).

evidence.claim: Earth's rotational speed is about 1,674.7 km/h (465.2 m/s) at the equator, decreasing to zero at the poles.

traceability.purpose: Equator: a low close-up along the equator of the stopped globe; one long east arrow carries the cited equatorial speed (1,674.7 km/h).

evidence.claim: Earth's rotational speed is about 1,674.7 km/h (465.2 m/s) at the equator, decreasing to zero at the poles.

traceability.purpose: Forces: a free-body view over the sliding ground: gravity (9.8 m/s²) pulls straight down while the sideways speed stays; the two arrows are different quantities and are labelled with their own units.

evidence.claim: Near Earth's surface, the acceleration due to gravity is 9.8 m/s2.
Earth's rotational speed is about 1,674.7 km/h (465.2 m/s) at the equator, decreasing to zero at the poles.

traceability.purpose: Slide: a wide shot from the surface: the ground and everything fixed to it rush backwards under a person who still carries the old speed; only contact with the ground can slow them.

evidence.claim: Earth's rotational speed is about 1,674.7 km/h (465.2 m/s) at the equator, decreasing to zero at the poles.

traceability.purpose: Latitude: the 45° parallel is drawn on the real globe beside the equator; each carries an east arrow whose length is cos(latitude) of the equator's, labelled with the cited speeds (1,184.2 km/h, 1,674.7 km/h).

evidence.claim: At 45° latitude, the speed is roughly 1,184.2 km/h.
Earth's rotational speed is about 1,674.7 km/h (465.2 m/s) at the equator, decreasing to zero at the poles.

traceability.purpose: Payoff: the camera tilts over the North Pole while arrows on each parallel shrink as cos(latitude) to nothing at the pole: the claim 'gentle near the poles' is seen, not read.

evidence.claim: Earth's rotational speed is about 1,674.7 km/h (465.2 m/s) at the equator, decreasing to zero at the poles.
